served.stem: Lone pairs on central P in PCl₃?
served.bankWhy: P has 5 valence; 3 P−Cl bonds use 3, leaving 2 e⁻ = 1 LP.

answer.line: P brings 5 valence electrons, spends 3 on bonds, and keeps 2 as one lone pair.

steps: Count the central atom first. P is in group 15, so it brings 5 valence electrons.
Spend them on bonds. Three P-Cl single bonds use 3 of the 5.
What is left becomes lone pairs: 5 - 3 = 2 electrons, which is 1 pair. That pair is why PCl3 is a pyramid and not flat.

choices.note: 0 fits BF3, where B brings only 3 electrons. P brings 5, so 2 are left after 3 bonds.
2 is the leftover electron count. Two electrons make one pair.
3 is the bonding pairs on P, and the lone pairs on each Cl. The stem asks for lone pairs on P.
9 pairs on the chlorines plus 1 on P is 10. Only the central atom was asked.
